bayesnec support in toxval

Source: BAYESNEC-human.md

toxval stopped accepting models fitted with bayesnec in phase 3, when its methods for them were deleted. The work set out here restores that support. It covers what will be built, why, what a user will see, and the order of the work.

The detail is in BAYESNEC-claude.md, which uses the same section numbers: the function calls, the measurements, the edge cases and the rejected alternatives. Each decision is stated in full there. Here each is given with a short reason and a pointer.

REFACTOR-human.md is the plan this one amends. It is assumed to have been read.

1. The decision

toxval will contain the toxval_predict() methods for fits made with bayesnec. ecx() and nsec() will then accept a bnec() fit again, as they did before phase 3. RF and AP agreed this on 2026-10-23. It is proposed in #68 and will be recorded as decision T35.

The reason is that a toxval_pred needs facts that toxval defines and bayesnec has no use for. Examples are the keys table that names each curve, x_control, the lowest concentration in the data, and the equation that produced each realisation of a model-averaged fit. If bayesnec wrote these, any change to the toxval_pred contract would need a release of both packages, in the right order.

The decision replaces phase 7 of REFACTOR-human.md and the split recorded on #39. That split put the methods in bayesnec, with bayesnec importing toxval. It required toxval to be published on CRAN before bayesnec could use it. That requirement no longer applies, because bayesnec no longer needs to import toxval. Publication on CRAN (phase 6) therefore no longer has to come before bayesnec support.

The decision does not change the compute functions or the toxval tibble. The toxval_pred contract gains two optional metadata elements (section 3.4). BAYESNEC-claude.md §1 lists every passage in the plan documents and on the issues that the decision overrides.

2. Changes for a user

A user can pass a bnec() fit to ecx(), nsec() or toxval_predict(), and gets a toxval tibble, as for a brms or drc fit:

library(bayesnec)
fit <- bnec(y ~ crf(x, model = "nec4param"), data = nec_data)

toxval::ecx(fit, proportion = 0.1)
toxval::nsec(manec_example)
toxval::nsec(manec_example, anchor = "component")

The header of the result names the class, for example # Model: bayesmanecfit. The columns are those of REFACTOR-human.md §3.1.

bayesnec must be installed, because it builds the grid of concentrations the curve is predicted on (section 3.1). A user with a bnec() fit will normally have it installed.

The estimates are on the scale of the predictor named in crf(). For crf(log(x), ...) the result is in units of x. bayesnec::ecx() currently reports the same fit in units of log(x), with a message. So xform = exp must not be supplied for a transformation written inside crf(). A predictor that was transformed into its own column before fitting is reported on that column’s scale, as it is now. bayesnec decision D41 makes its own functions report on the recorded scale from version 3.0. BAYESNEC-claude.md §2.1 gives the mechanism.

The aligned defaults use each equation’s control for a model average (T12), the amended no-crossing rule (T21), and a 500-point grid (T31). toxval also reports the increasing direction as a separate row (T10), whereas bayesnec reports the decreasing direction. The packages retain different output shapes and explicit options; matching values still require matching those options.

Under type = "absolute", the decreasing ECx should agree with bayesnec realisation by realisation. Task 5 tests that.

A call to ecx() or nsec() without a package prefix can reach bayesnec’s function of the same name instead (section 3.6).

3. Design decisions

3.1 Sources of the grid and the curves

bayesnec supplies the prediction grid. toxval computes the curves itself from the brmsfit objects stored inside the fit (BAYESNEC-claude.md §3.1).

The grid comes from bayesnec::bnec_newdata(), which is exported and is in the CRAN release. It sets the number of trials to 1 for a binomial fit, and an exposure denominator to 1 for a rate, so that the curve is a proportion or a rate. Copying those rules into toxval would mean keeping two copies in step.

The curves come from brms::posterior_epred() called on the brmsfit stored in the object, with group-level effects marginalised. On the nec4param equation of manec_example, over a 50-point grid, this gave a matrix identical to bayesnec’s own prediction.

bayesnec is added to Suggests (section 6). The methods stop with a message when it is not installed, and their tests are skipped.

3.2 Model-averaged fits

For a bayesmanecfit, toxval builds one model-averaged curve matrix from the same draws that bayesnec uses. It also records which equation produced each realisation (BAYESNEC-claude.md §3.2).

bayesnec keeps a number of draws from each equation in proportion to its model weight. The list of draws kept from each equation is what bayesnec calls the draw index. It is stored on the object. An object saved before bayesnec 2.1.3.7 has none, and bayesnec rebuilds it from a fixed seed. toxval uses the stored index, or rebuilds it by the same rule.

This was checked on manec_example, with bayesnec 2.1.3.39 and a 50-point grid. The matrix built by toxval was identical to bayesnec::posterior_epred(). It held 100 realisations: 83 from nec4param and 17 from ecx4param. Realisation i is therefore the same draw in both packages. A bayesnec plot and a toxval estimate then describe the same posterior.

Recording the equation of each realisation is what anchor = "component" requires (REFACTOR-human.md §3.8). A bayesmanecfit is the first class for which "component" and "model" give different answers.

Under "component", toxval takes each equation’s reference from every draw of that equation’s fit, as bayesnec does. A reference is the 1% point of the control responses, so it is estimated best from all the draws available. toxval_predict() already predicts every draw of every equation before keeping those in the average. It now also keeps each draw’s control response, in meta$model_control. On manec_example at sig_val = 0.01, the decreasing NSEC is 1.474 (0.766, 1.551) in both packages.

The first implementation used only each equation’s draws in the average, which on manec_example is 17 draws for ecx4param. Its lower limit was 0.18 below bayesnec’s. A 1% point estimated from few draws lies nearer the middle of the control responses on average, and it lowered every ecx4param NSEC by 0.05 to 0.20. RF reversed the ruling that accepted this on 2026-10-29 (BAYESNEC-claude.md §3.2).

3.3 Classes in the first pull request

The first pull request covers bayesnecfit and bayesmanecfit. These are the two classes in the CRAN release of bayesnec. Every other bayesnec class stops with a message naming the class (BAYESNEC-claude.md §3.3).

Two terms are used in the table. A two-part family, such as hurdle_gamma, models the zeros separately from the positive values, so one fit describes two curves. A bayesnechurdlefit holds two separate fits, one for survival and one for growth among survivors.

class on CRAN in the first PR what support needs
bayesnecfit yes yes —
bayesmanecfit yes yes —
bayesnecfit with a two-part family such as hurdle_gamma no no an argument choosing which part of the response to report
bayesnechurdlefit no no an argument choosing growth, survival or their product
bayesnecgroupfit no no a change to toxval_pred (below)
bayesnecjointfit no no a change to toxval_pred (below)

A bayesnecgroupfit is a separate fit for each level of a factor, such as one fit per site. Each level is predicted over its own concentrations. A bayesnecjointfit is one fit across levels, and since bayesnec decision D40 each level is also read over its own concentrations. A toxval_pred has one grid and one control concentration for every curve. Supporting these classes therefore needs a decision on whether a toxval_pred can hold a grid per curve.

The four classes not in the first pull request exist only on bayesnec’s development branches, and bayesnecjointfit changed this month. Each will get its own pull request once it is released.

3.4 Additions to toxval_pred

meta gains three optional elements, and no new slot is added (BAYESNEC-claude.md §3.4).

  • meta$draw_model names the equation that produced each realisation.
  • meta$model_weights gives the model weight of each equation in the set.
  • meta$model_control holds the control response of each equation in every draw of its fit, including the draws left out of the average.

The second makes the equations behind a model-averaged estimate recoverable from the result, as REFACTOR-claude.md §3.10 requires. The third sets the references under anchor = "component" (section 3.2). All three are checked when present. toxval_pred is public interface, so all three are documented with the rest of the metadata.

Two existing slots are filled from the fit:

  • The asymptote slot, which phase 4 adds (decision T24), takes the bot parameter for the nine equations that have one. It takes 0 for an equation without bot, whose curve tends to zero. It is NA for a gaussian fit of such an equation, since that family has no lower bound.
  • The threshold slot stays empty. The NEC, the nec parameter, exists only in the ten equations whose names begin nec. In a model-averaged set it is therefore missing for some realisations. Deciding what that means is the question #25 is open for.

A binomial or beta-binomial bnec() fit is predicted with one trial. Its curve is therefore a proportion, bounded at 1, and the increasing absolute reference uses that bound (decision T18).

3.5 bayesnec behaviour not reproduced

Four behaviours of bayesnec are not reproduced (BAYESNEC-claude.md §3.5).

  • The back-transformation of a predictor transformed inside crf() (decision T6, section 2).
  • The refusal of an absolute ECx for a gaussian fit of an equation without bot. bayesnec has itself removed it, following OECD TG 201. The guard listed in REFACTOR-claude.md §3.7 is deleted.
  • The computation of each metric per equation followed by mixing of the results. toxval computes every metric on the one model-averaged matrix (section 3.2).
  • The decline from the peak, hormesis_def = "max", which defines a different reference (decision T28).

3.6 The shared function names

This work documents the name conflict between the two packages and changes nothing in bayesnec (BAYESNEC-claude.md §3.6).

bayesnec exports ecx() and nsec(), with methods for its own classes and copies of nsec() for brmsfit and drc fits. When bayesnec is attached after toxval, ecx() on a brmsfit stops with “no applicable method”. With the other attach order, ecx() on a bnec() fit runs toxval’s definition. Neither order gives a warning.

What bayesnec does about its own ecx() and nsec() is for bayesnec to decide. Its plan currently relocates them to toxval and imports toxval (bayesnec decision D10 and issue #255). That plan is no longer needed for toxval to support bayesnec fits.

4. Order of work

There are six tasks, and all six are done. Task 0 was done last, after PR #66 merged. BAYESNEC-claude.md §4 gives files, tests and stopping points for each.

  1. Task 0 records the decision. It adds T35 to notes/implementation/02_decisions.md, rewrites phases 6 and 7 of the refactor plan, and drafts a decision comment for #39. It is needed so that the plan of record and the issue agree with this document. It waits for PR #66 to merge, because #66 edits the same refactor documents and adds T34. It is done when no passage listed in BAYESNEC-claude.md §1 still places the methods in bayesnec.
  2. Task 1 stores the test fits. It adds manec_example, a binomial fit and a fit with crf(log(x)) to tests/testthat/fixtures/, with the code that made them in data-raw/. The tests need a model-averaged fit, a binomial response predicted as a proportion, and a predictor transformed inside crf(), and no stored fit has these. Their size is not limited during development. It is done when the fixtures load and data-raw/DATASET.R records the bayesnec version.
  3. Task 2 adds the single-fit method, toxval_predict.bayesnecfit(), with the check that bayesnec is installed and the refusal of the other classes. It is done when its curves are identical to bayesnec’s on every fixture and each refusal is tested.
  4. Task 3 adds the model-averaged method, toxval_predict.bayesmanecfit(), and the two meta elements. It is done when its matrix is identical to bayesnec::posterior_epred() on manec_example and the call leaves the caller’s random number state unchanged.
  5. Task 4 fills the asymptote slot and makes anchor = "component" read meta$draw_model and meta$model_control. It is done when type = "relative" and both anchors are tested on manec_example.
  6. Task 5 tests ecx() and nsec() on every fixture and compares them with bayesnec in tests/local/. It also updates the examples, the README and DESCRIPTION. It waits for task 4. It is done when R CMD check passes with and without bayesnec installed.

The four classes of section 3.3 follow in later pull requests.

5. Branch

The work is on phase-7-bayesnec-methods. PR #66 has merged into phase-2. The branch is built on PR #78, which starts every grid at the control concentration (#73) and has merged into phase-2. The pull request goes into phase-2, and is merged before #77, the documentation review (BAYESNEC-claude.md §5).

6. Decisions and points for review

RF decided three of these.

  • bayesnec is added to Suggests (section 3.1; 2026-10-23).
  • Under anchor = "component" each equation’s reference is taken over every draw of its fit, so toxval matches bayesnec (section 3.2). RF decided this on 2026-10-29, reversing the ruling of 2026-10-23 that accepted the difference from using the draws in the average alone.
  • Fixture size does not limit this work (2026-10-23), because the tests are needed during development and CRAN submission is not near. When the package is prepared for CRAN, a fit needed only by the tests in tests/local/ can be kept out of the built package, as bayesnec does (BAYESNEC-claude.md §4, task 1).

The rest are proposed rather than decided, and each is argued in the section named.

  • Using bayesnec’s own draw index for a model-averaged fit (section 3.2).
  • Limiting the first pull request to two classes (section 3.3).
  • Leaving threshold empty until #25 (section 3.4).
  • Reporting a predictor transformed inside crf() on its recorded scale (section 2).
